title: Encryption retention simulator and proof-diff exporter
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a simulator and export tool that takes tenant retention policies, regional residency bounds, and key rotation schedules and produces: 1) a timeline-based simulation of which key versions would have encrypted which tenant artifacts over time; 2) a compact, signable 'proof-diff' bundle showing the delta between two retention/rotation states for auditor consumption. The tool should support HSM-backed signing (via KMS/HSM signing endpoint) and emit human-readable CSV/NDJSON and a machine-checkable bundle (signed manifest + index). This enables on-demand forensic snapshots for audits without forcing full re-encryption or heavy scans of object stores.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts: retention policy JSON, key rotation schedule (ISO timestamps), and region-to-tenant mapping and produces a per-tenant timeline of encrypted object ranges
Proof-diff exporter produces a signed bundle containing: manifest.json, edge-diff.ndjson, and provenance.log and is verifiable using the KMS public key
End-to-end test runs in CI using the HSM test harness and shows signatures can be validated against the test KMS key
Simulator can reason about cross-region eventual consistency windows (configurable window, default 30s) and flags potential gaps in evidence
Performance: simulation for a tenant with 10M objects completes within 5 minutes in the prototype using sampling heuristics and produces a bounded-size diff (<=50MB for typical production tenants)
UX: Console has a new Audit snapshot page that can request a simulator run and download a proof bundle (linked via pre-signed URL)
updates: 2025-02-15 - Ticket created by Aisha. Initial design sketch attached, focusing on avoiding full scans by using key usage indices and object metadata sampling.

2025-02-20 - Spike complete: prototype that replays rotation schedule against a synthetic object timeline exists. Found that object store modification timestamps are noisy in some regions; added normalization step.

2025-02-24 - Design review with Security and PM: agreed on bundle structure (manifest.json + ndjson edges + provenance.log). Security requested HSM-signed manifest and rotation-proof chain that includes KMS-key fingerprints.

2025-02-26 - Implementation: initial simulator library up at //github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/feat/retention-sim (PR pending). Added sample dataset generator and sampling heuristics (LSH-based shard sampling) to keep runtime bounded.

2025-03-01 - Blocker noted: HSM test harness needs an API to produce ephemeral signer tokens for CI. Filing dependency ENG-97455 to add ephemeral HSM test-token service for CI signing. Miguel assigned to unblock with infra.

2025-03-01 - Added Console mock for Audit snapshot flow; UX feedback from PM suggests adding an opt-in 'include storage-level checksums' toggle to increase verifier confidence. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-01 - Next: complete PR, add HSM CI token, integrate bundle upload to S3 with short-lived link, and add e2e verification job in GitHub Actions.
risks: HSM signing latency or CI access could delay automated e2e verification — mitigated by having a test-mode signed bundle using a test key registered in the console
Simulator sampling heuristics may produce false negatives for low-volume tenants; plan to surface confidence scores in the manifest
Large tenants could produce proof bundles that are expensive to store/transfer; we will enforce size limits and provide streaming download options
Cross-region clock skew could cause misattribution of key versions; simulator will include adjusted windowing and a flagged uncertainty field
